# Pre-process




## Features


The pre-trained model we are using has sentiment labels as: 0=negaticve, 1=neutral, 2=positive.  Since our dataset is labeled negative, neutral, and positive, we will convert them to integer values corresponding to the pre-trained model.




```{python}


nyt_sentiments = nytComments17_sentiments.copy()


```





```{python}



rename_map={
    "negative": 0,
    "neutral": 1,
    "positive": 2
}




```


```{python}

pd.set_option('future.no_silent_downcasting', True)


```

```{python}


nyt_sentiments['sentiment'] = nytComments17_sentiments ['sentiment'].replace(rename_map)



```

We will also rename the columns sentiment and commentBody to reflect those used in the pre-trained model

```{python}


nyt_comments_dict = {"commentBody":"text", "sentiment":"label"}


```

```{python}

nyt_sentiments = nyt_sentiments.rename(columns={"commentBody":"text", "sentiment":"label"})



```

```{python}

nyt_sentiments.info()



```


Columns not required for fine tuning and prediction will be dropped



```{python}


nyt_sentiments=nyt_sentiments.drop(columns=['commentID', 'typeOfMaterial', 'newDesk'], axis=1)

```

Create class for custom dataset. 

```{python}

class NYTDataset(torch.utils.data.Dataset):
    def __init__(self, encodings, labels):
        self.encodings = encodings
        self.labels = labels

    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        item = {key: torch.tensor(val[idx])
            for key, val in self.encodings.items()}
        item['labels'] = torch.tensor(self.labels[idx])
        return item
    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.labels)


```
